title: Isaiah 29
paragraphs: ¹ Woe to Ariel, to Ariel, the city where David camped! Add year to year; let the cycle of feasts go on. ² Yet I will besiege Ariel, and there will be mourning and sorrow, and it will truly become an Ariel — an altar hearth of God — to me. ³ I will encamp against you on all sides; I will besiege you with towers and raise up siege works against you. ⁴ Brought low, you will speak from the ground; your words will come mumbling out of the dust. Your voice will come like that of a ghost from the earth, your words whispering from the dust. ⁵ But the hordes of your enemies will become like fine dust, the hordes of the ruthless like driven chaff. And suddenly, in an instant,

⁶ you will be visited by the LORD of hosts with thunder, earthquake, and great noise, with whirlwind and tempest and devouring flames. ⁷ The hordes of all the nations that fight against Ariel — all who wage war against her, besiege her, and distress her — will be like a dream, like a vision in the night. ⁸ It will be like a hungry man who dreams he is eating, but wakes up empty; or like a thirsty man who dreams he is drinking, but wakes up faint and parched with thirst. So it will be with the hordes of all the nations that fight against Mount Zion. ⁹ Stagger and be dazed! Blind yourselves and stay blind! Be drunk, but not with wine; stagger, but not from strong drink. ¹⁰ For the LORD has poured over you a spirit of deep sleep. He has shut your eyes — the prophets — and covered your heads — the seers.

¹¹ For you this whole vision has become like the words of a sealed book. People hand it to someone who can read and say, "Please read this." But that person answers, "I can't — it is sealed." ¹² Or the book is handed to someone who cannot read and they are told, "Please read this." That person answers, "I don't know how to read." ¹³ The Lord says: "These people approach me with their mouths and honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me. Their worship of me is made up of human rules they have been taught. ¹⁴ Therefore, I will once more astound these people with wonder upon wonder. The wisdom of the wise will perish, and the intelligence of the intelligent will vanish." ¹⁵ Woe to those who hide their plans from the LORD, who do their work in darkness and think, "Who sees us? Who will know?"

¹⁶ How confused you are! Is the potter no better than the clay? Shall what is made say to its maker, "He did not make me"? Can a pot say to the potter, "He knows nothing"? ¹⁷ In a very short time, won't Lebanon be turned into a fruitful orchard, and won't the fruitful orchard be regarded as a forest? ¹⁸ In that day the deaf will hear the words of a book, and out of gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind will see. ¹⁹ The meek will find new joy in the LORD, and the poorest of the poor will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel. ²⁰ For the ruthless will vanish, the mockers will disappear, and all who are eager to do evil will be cut off —

²¹ those who convict a person on a false charge, who ensnare the defender at the gate, and who deny justice to the innocent. ²² Therefore this is what the LORD says to the house of Jacob — the LORD who redeemed Abraham: "Jacob will no longer be ashamed, no longer will his face grow pale. ²³ When he sees his children, the work of my hands, in his midst, they will honor my name. They will acknowledge the holiness of the Holy One of Jacob, and will stand in awe of the God of Israel. ²⁴ Those who in spirit go astray will come to understanding, and those who complain will accept instruction."
